component_evidence.label: Platform / foundation
component_evidence.source_note: Foundation geometry and site loads require design; Ontario tiny-home guidance confirms footing/foundation and anchorage review. Structural base and floor framing exclude finish flooring.

component_evidence.label: Yurt frame and tension structure
component_evidence.source_note: Canadian yurt supplier specifications support diameter, lattice, rafters, crown/dome and cable as distinct physical elements; this row is limited to the wall/tension system and structural sizing remains engineered.

component_evidence.label: Roof structure and covering
component_evidence.source_note: Actual sloping roof area is calculated from radius and roof pitch; this row covers the pitched roof structure and covering, not wall air/water control.

component_evidence.label: Insulation
component_evidence.source_note: Ontario guidance requires year-round energy efficiency and insulation; exact assembly requires envelope design.

component_evidence.label: Weatherproofing and air control
component_evidence.source_note: Water, moisture and draft control are required design outcomes; this row covers wall air/water control, flashing and sealing and excludes the roof covering.

component_evidence.label: Windows / dome glazing
component_evidence.source_note: Canadian suppliers publish standard window/dome options and limits; thermal performance and framing are design-specific.

component_evidence.label: Exterior and interior doors
component_evidence.source_note: Canadian yurt supplier standard door and jamb packages provide a market-spec reference; installed code-compliant openings require confirmation.

component_evidence.label: Interior finishes and floor finish
component_evidence.source_note: Open-plan finish allowance; this row covers finish flooring, partitions and surfaces, not structural platform/floor framing. Material choice and moisture detailing require a design.

component_evidence.label: Upper-floor structure and load path
component_evidence.source_note: Two-storey/loft structure requires span, support, connection and foundation engineering; diameter alone cannot establish feasibility.

component_evidence.label: Stairs and access opening
component_evidence.source_note: Stairs, guards and opening are included as separate upper-floor consequences; code review required.

component_evidence.label: Loft guards / edge protection
component_evidence.source_note: Guard geometry is layout-specific and requires building-code confirmation.

component_evidence.label: Additional kitchen fit-out
component_evidence.source_note: Keeps only additional cabinetry, counters, appliances and kitchen finishes outside the inclusive plumbing package. Itemization and appliance/installation quotes remain required; sink, faucet and utility connections are excluded here.

component_evidence.label: Additional bathroom fit-out
component_evidence.source_note: Keeps only additional bathroom finishes, storage and non-plumbing fit-out outside the inclusive water/plumbing/sanitation package. Itemization and approval remain required; toilet, shower and plumbing fixtures are excluded here.

component_evidence.label: Heating appliance and system
component_evidence.source_note: Existing ARC winter masonry-heater concept; appliance, chimney/fire safety and installation require design confirmation.

component_evidence.label: Ventilation / air exchange
component_evidence.source_note: Ontario guidance recommends HVAC appropriate to small year-round spaces; system selection requires design.

component_evidence.label: Household electrical equipment
component_evidence.source_note: Existing ARC approximately 400 Wh/day, 400 W PV, MPPT, 2.52 kWh nominal flooded lead-acid storage and 1,000 W pure-sine inverter; inclusive package labour and inspection allowance are decomposed in the service-package record.

component_evidence.label: Water, plumbing and sanitation package
component_evidence.source_note: Inclusive ARC package: fixtures, toilet, excavation, compact plumbing, commissioning, included qualified plumbing labour and permit allowance are counted once in the package total.

component_evidence.label: Domestic hot water package
component_evidence.source_note: Inclusive ARC winter thermosiphon and summer solar-thermal package; integration labour is included once in the package total.

component_evidence.label: Household demand upgrade
component_evidence.source_note: Explicit allowance for larger household storage, fixtures and electrical demand; replace with a design takeoff.

component_evidence.label: Delivery and logistics
component_evidence.source_note: Distance, access, crane/hauling and seasonal road conditions require a quotation.

component_evidence.label: Equipment hire
component_evidence.source_note: Lifting, access and foundation equipment vary with site and layout.

component_evidence.label: Design and engineering
component_evidence.source_note: Yurt structural system, snow/wind loads, fire separation, envelope, foundation and servicing require qualified design.

component_evidence.label: Permits and approvals
component_evidence.source_note: Ontario requires building permits for tiny homes; local permit/development fees depend on the approving municipality and project.

inclusion_rules: The selected yurt supplier package is one purchased package; its included installation is visible but never added as another labour row.
The supplier package excludes the platform, utilities, delivery and climate-control systems; those are separately itemized.
A material catalog row may be used once per BOM line. Package-included lattice, rafters, ring, cable, covers and insulation are never priced again by additional assemblies.
The historical ARC 61,000 figure is comparison-only and cannot calibrate or supply a current component rate.

accounting_rules: A component is assigned one physical driver and appears once in the completed dwelling total.

The ARC household utility package is carried forward once as water/plumbing/sanitation 5,940 CAD, hot water 2,000 CAD and electrical 3,300 CAD. Included paid labour and fees are decomposed for audit but are not added again.
Centralized servicing removes the corresponding household component from resident dwelling capital and exposes the unresolved cost as a shared-infrastructure quotation requirement.
Owner labour reduces upfront cash but remains visible as owner hours and imputed value; professional work is not treated as owner-replaceable.
Taxes and contingency are explicit additions. They are not used to force agreement with the legacy CAD 61,000 benchmark.
A custom completed-dwelling quote overrides financing headline value but leaves the modelled component ledger and unallocated quote difference visible.
